name: queries/admin.py
summary: Django admin configuration registering QueryFeedback, QueryHistory, and QueryResult models with custom ModelAdmin classes.
purpose: Provides a built-in administrative interface so operations and support teams can view, search, filter, and manage query-related domain data—user feedback, execution history, and result sets—without requiring custom internal tools or direct database access.
responsibilities: Register QueryFeedback, QueryHistory, and QueryResult models with the Django admin site
Define admin-specific presentation, searchability, and behavior for query domain entities
Enable authorized staff to perform CRUD and audit operations on query metadata and user feedback
Act as a thin adapter between the queries app ORM models and Django's contrib.admin framework
inputs: QueryFeedback, QueryHistory, and QueryResult model classes
outputs: Registered admin interfaces for query-related models
Admin UI list, detail, create, update, and delete views
architecture_notes: Follows the standard Django ModelAdmin pattern, keeping administrative presentation logic isolated from business logic and API layers within the queries app boundary. Co-locating admin.py with the models it manages preserves high cohesion. The module functions as a declarative configuration layer that adapts domain entities to Django's built-in admin CMS capabilities without polluting model or serializer code.
improvements: Add explicit list_display, list_filter, and search_fields to each ModelAdmin to improve usability over default configurations
Override readonly_fields or get_queryset to prevent accidental mutation of immutable historical query execution records
Add fieldsets or inlines to improve detail page layout for complex query result and feedback objects
Introduce date_hierarchy on timestamp fields for temporal navigation of query history
Restrict admin access or add object-level permissions if query data contains PII or sensitive user-generated content
